text.p: Bonds gained in line with a stronger Europe and traders expected the local market to keep pace with any further advances abroad on Wednesday after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan indicated no U.S. rate rise was on the way.
Greenspan said on Tuesday night that there were signs that the pace of U.S. economic growth was slowing.
"The market has the strength to accompany Europe, with the gains possibly being extended during the session," said one trader.
With attention focused on the longer end, there was a tendency for the curve to flatten slightly, they added.
The gap between the two year bond and the 10 year stood at 102 basis points against 106 at Tuesday's close.
